**Actionable comments posted: 7**
🤖 Fix all issues with AI agents ``` In `@pmoves/tools/chit_manifest_sync.py`: - Around line 18-29: CANONICAL_SOURCE_ALIASES currently maps SERVICE_PASSWORD_POSTGRES and SERVICE_PASSWORD_ADMIN to the exact same alias tuple ("POSTGRES_PASSWORD", "SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD"), which will create overlapping v1 alias lists; either consolidate those two keys into a single canonical key if they are the same secret, or give them distinct alias tuples so they do not overlap (e.g., adjust the tuple for SERVICE_PASSWORD_ADMIN or SERVICE_PASSWORD_POSTGRES), updating the CANONICAL_SOURCE_ALIASES mapping accordingly and ensuring any resolution logic that uses CANONICAL_SOURCE_ALIASES still finds the intended alias names. - Line 10: Create the missing requirements file pmoves/tools/requirements-lite.txt and list the tool dependencies required by scripts in pmoves/tools (at minimum add PyYAML>=6.0 to satisfy the import yaml used in chit_manifest_sync.py and the other tools), and include any other common runtime deps referenced by those tools; ensure bootstrap_light_env.py’s default requirement path is satisfied by this new requirements-lite.txt so pip install -r pmoves/tools/requirements-lite.txt will install the necessary packages. In `@pmoves/tools/runner_lane_map.py`: - Around line 363-370: The code currently sets strict_fail = bool(unmapped) unconditionally causing unmapped lanes to force exit code 2 even when args.strict is False; change the logic so strict_fail starts False and only considers unmapped when args.strict is True (i.e., if args.strict then strict_fail = strict_fail or bool(unmapped)), while preserving the existing handling of args.enforce_phase, args.enforce_phase -> phase_failures, and unavailable so that strict_fail is only true when the user requested strict behavior; keep the final if strict_fail: return 2. - Around line 90-100: discover_groups currently only globs "*.yml" and will miss workflows with a ".yaml" extension; update discover_groups to scan both "*.yml" and "*.yaml" (e.g., iterate over both glob patterns or combine results) so every workflow file is inspected, then continue using RUNS_ON_LIST_RE and normalize_group as before to collect groups; ensure duplicates are still deduplicated in the groups set before returning the sorted list. In `@pmoves/tools/runtime_secrets_hydrate.py`: - Around line 161-183: The calls to set_if_missing for MEILI_MASTER_KEY, FIREFLY_APP_KEY, and AGENT_ZERO_EVENTS_TOKEN silently generate random tokens via secrets.token_urlsafe when no container/env value exists; change each call site to first compute the candidate value and a boolean flag (e.g., is_generated = True when both _find_container_env_value(...) and env_values.get(...) are empty and you fallback to secrets.token_urlsafe(...)), then call set_if_missing with the value and, if is_generated, emit a warning log entry (use the existing module logger) that includes the secret name (e.g., "MEILI_MASTER_KEY"), a short marker like "[AUTO-GENERATED-PLACEHOLDER]", and that the value was generated as a placeholder so operators can distinguish hydrated vs generated secrets; keep the rest of the logic (calls to _find_container_env_value, env_values.get, and secrets.token_urlsafe) unchanged. In `@pmoves/tools/showtime_watch.py`: - Around line 82-89: The loop in showtime_watch.py currently returns 0 on timeout or when STOP is set, which masks failures; change the exit codes so that successful readiness (when collect returns rows all OK) returns 0, but the timeout path and STOP-triggered path return a non-zero code (e.g., 1). Concretely, update the loop surrounding collect(), render_plain(), and the STOP/max_seconds check to return 1 on exit due to timeout or STOP (and mirror the same change for the Rich-render loop around render_rich at lines ~118-122), leaving the existing return 0 only for the all-ready condition so callers can distinguish success from timeout/stop. - Around line 70-79: The collect function can call ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=0 when ENDPOINTS is empty; add a guard at the top of collect to return an empty list if ENDPOINTS is falsy (e.g., if not ENDPOINTS: return []), or alternatively compute workers = max(1, min(24, len(ENDPOINTS))) so ThreadPoolExecutor never receives 0; update the code paths around ThreadPoolExecutor/ probe/ futs accordingly to use the non-zero worker count or early return. ```
🧹 Nitpick comments (13)
pmoves/tools/runtime_secrets_hydrate.py (2)
`18-30`: **`_parse_env_file` does not strip values, unlike `parse_env_file` in `secrets_hardening_audit.py`.** Line 29 stores the raw value after `=` without stripping, while the nearly identical `parse_env_file` in `secrets_hardening_audit.py` (line 45) does `.strip()` on both key and value. Callers in this file compensate by calling `.strip()` at every access site (e.g., lines 134, 143–157, 166, 174), but this is fragile and duplicative. Consider stripping here for consistency or extracting a shared env-parsing helper across the two modules.
♻️ Strip values at parse time for consistency ```diff key = key.strip() if key: - values[key] = value + values[key] = value.strip() return values ```
--- `33-54`: **`_write_env_file` reads the file then writes it back without any atomicity safeguard.** If the process crashes mid-write, `path.write_text(text, ...)` can truncate the env file. For a secrets-related file this could be painful. Consider writing to a temporary file in the same directory and then using `os.replace()` for an atomic rename.
🛡️ Atomic write pattern ```diff +import tempfile + def _write_env_file(path: Path, updates: Mapping[str, str]) -> None: path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").splitlines() if path.exists() else [] ... text = "\n".join(lines) if text and not text.endswith("\n"): text += "\n" - path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8") + fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=".tmp") + try: + os.write(fd, text.encode("utf-8")) + os.close(fd) + os.replace(tmp, path) + except BaseException: + os.close(fd) if not os.get_inheritable(fd) else None + Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True) + raise ```
pmoves/tools/showtime_watch.py (2)
`19-21`: **Fragile `sys.path` manipulation for sibling import.** Inserting `sys.path[0]` at module scope is a common pattern for Make-invoked scripts, but it can shadow stdlib or third-party modules if the `tools/` directory happens to contain a file with a colliding name. A relative import or `importlib` approach would be more robust, though this is acceptable for operator tooling. --- `24-29`: **Global `STOP` flag is not declared as `threading`-safe.** The `STOP` bool is written by the signal handler and read by the main-thread loop. In CPython this works due to the GIL, but it's technically a data race per the language model. A `threading.Event` would be more correct and still simple.
pmoves/tools/bootstrap_light_env.py (2)
`56-57`: **`run()` propagates `CalledProcessError` with no context.** When a subprocess fails, the traceback includes the raw command but not which step (venv creation vs. pip install) failed. Adding a brief wrapper or context message would improve operator UX. --- `30-34`: **`action="append"` with a non-`None` default accumulates values rather than replacing the default.** If a user passes `--requirements custom.txt`, argparse appends to the default, yielding `["tools/requirements-lite.txt", "custom.txt"]`. Since the lite requirements are always included, this should be documented in the help text to clarify intent. If users should be able to replace the default entirely, use `default=None` and handle it in code.
💡 Option A: document the behavior; Option B: use None default ```diff parser.add_argument( "--requirements", action="append", - default=["tools/requirements-lite.txt"], - help="Requirements file(s) relative to pmoves/ (repeatable).", + default=None, + help="Requirements file(s) relative to pmoves/ (repeatable; always includes tools/requirements-lite.txt unless overridden).", ) ``` Then in `main()`: ```diff - req_files = [resolve_under_pmoves(item) for item in args.requirements] + reqs = args.requirements or ["tools/requirements-lite.txt"] + req_files = [resolve_under_pmoves(item) for item in reqs] ```
pmoves/tools/secrets_hardening_audit.py (2)
`27-36`: **`candidate_files()` does a full recursive scan of the repo root.** This is fine for an audit tool, but on very large repos `rglob("*")` can be slow. If performance becomes an issue, consider using `git ls-files` to restrict to tracked files only, which also avoids scanning build artifacts. --- `39-46`: **`parse_env_file` and `is_placeholder` duplicate logic from `runtime_secrets_hydrate.py`.** Both modules have their own env-parsing and placeholder-detection functions with slightly different semantics (e.g., stripping behavior, placeholder token sets). Consider extracting a shared `env_utils` module under `pmoves/tools/` to avoid drift. Also applies to: 49-62
pmoves/tools/local_cert_runners.py (2)
`86-110`: **Docker socket mount grants the runner container full host Docker access.** Line 107 (`/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock`) is standard for self-hosted GitHub runners that need Docker-in-Docker capability, but it's effectively root-equivalent access to the host's Docker daemon. Ensure this is documented in operator runbooks and that the runner image is pinned or verified. --- `193-203`: **`main()` signature takes `argv: list[str]` but `Sequence[str]` would be more flexible.** Other scripts in this PR use `Sequence[str] | None` for their `main` signatures. Minor inconsistency.
pmoves/tools/runner_lane_map.py (1)
`130-148`: **`load_runners` fetches only the first page (100 runners) without pagination.** Line 131 uses `per_page=100` but doesn't follow pagination links. If the repo has >100 runners, some will be missed and `lane_online` checks could give false negatives. For most local-cert setups this is fine, but consider using `gh api --paginate` (as done in `local_cert_runners.py` line 154) for consistency.
pmoves/tools/chit_manifest_sync.py (1)
`211-219`: **`--check` mode compares `yaml.safe_dump` output textually.** This works when the destination is always written by this tool (formatting is deterministic), but will report "out of sync" if the file was hand-edited with equivalent data in different formatting. This is probably the desired behavior (enforcing machine-generated output), but worth noting in the `--help` or a comment.
pmoves/tools/tooling_script_audit.py (1)
`272-279`: **Redundant `not union` guard in `jaccard()`.** Line 277 checks `if not union: return 0.0`, but this is unreachable — `a` and `b` are already confirmed non-empty on line 273, so their union is always non-empty.
♻️ Simplify ```diff def jaccard(a: set[str], b: set[str]) -> float: if not a or not b: return 0.0 - shared = a & b - union = a | b - if not union: - return 0.0 - return len(shared) / len(union) + return len(a & b) / len(a | b) ```
